verdicts.reproduction: Opened debate_arbitrator.md:203-204 (check reads `.problems` only; 'Fix each problem it lists'), :222-229 (step 8 has no check after `remember.sh decide`), :282 (DoD: 'debate-status.py lists no problem for it'); debate-status.py:379-384 (`vp, derived = ([], None) if stale else verdict_problems(...)`). Scratch: tests/lib/make_debate.py built a complete debate, then I set the verdict's request_sha to 0000000000000000: `--json` gave {status: stale, problems: [], gate: ['... request_sha differs ...']}, `--check` exit 2. Control with the transcript not yet written (the moment the arbitrator runs its step-7 check, before moderator step 9): correct sha -> problems ['verdict: no debate behind the verdict: missing t6.transcript.md']; mis-copied sha -> problems [] (status stale). Running `remember.sh decide` twice with one --link printed D-001 then D-002, both active.
verdicts.note: Holds as stated. The arbitrator's only self-check reads `.problems`, which the checker empties for a stale verdict, so a mis-copied REQUEST_SHA produces a cleaner result than a correct one (the correct-sha run still lists the not-yet-written transcript). Nothing re-checks after step 8, so a skipped `remember.sh decide` is first seen by the gate (promotion is reported in `.gate`, never in `.problems`). Rated MEDIUM, not HIGH: the gate does catch both states (`--check` exit 2) and the moderator's step 1 re-runs a stale debate on the 0c re-dispatch, so the consequence is a wasted arbitration or a blocked gate, not a wrong verdict shipped; under /autonomous a non-security blocker can be force-gated after three cycles (autonomous.md:342), which is the worst case. The hat's fix (check {status,problems}, repeat after step 8 reading `.gate`) is the right size.

verdicts.note: The text defect is real: the forbidden pattern contradicts the required step two lines above it and the moderator's own instruction, and the docs confirm the parameter does not exist in an interactive session. The claimed consequence is narrower than stated: eval.md:68 reconstructs the trajectory from execution logs, manifests and file ordering, none of which record Agent-call parameters, so a scorer following that rule cannot see whether `run_in_background` was passed and would penalise neither a correct interactive run nor a background spawn. The fact that this pattern is unscoreable from evidence at all is TEST-27's point, not a duplicate of this one.

verdicts.reproduction: Opened .claude/skills/core/develop-steps/step-0-orient.md:540-554 (guard 'applies to ALL agents spawned by this command'; exception names only backend_audit_agent and ui_audit_agent) and context-budget-protocol.md:50-56 (same guard, same exception). grep -rni paralysis .claude tests: the guard text lives only in those two skills plus codebase_mapper.md:93 and capability_flow_mapper.md:546 (their own copies); no command, hook or spawn template carries it, and develop.md:405 lists step-0-orient as a file the parent reads for Step 0. debate_moderator.md:113-117, 135-137, 144-152 enumerate what each child prompt carries; the guard isn't among them. No hook counts tool calls.
verdicts.note: The guard does conflict with read-heavy judges, and the exception list is incomplete, but the finding's scope and mechanism are narrower than stated. (1) It is not debate-specific: code_reviewer_I/II, security_reviewer, spec_impl_reconciler and every other reviewer read many files before their first write and are equally un-exempt, so the debate agents are a sliver of a general looseness in the guard. (2) The guard reaches a debate child only if the /develop parent pastes it into the moderator prompt and the moderator pastes it into its children's prompts, against the moderator's explicit list of what each child prompt carries; nothing automates that and no hook enforces a read count. Adding the debate agents (and reviewers) to the exception list is harmless and worth doing, but as written this is an instruction-consistency issue with no enforced behaviour behind it: LOW.

verdicts.reproduction: Opened debate_moderator.md:74-76 (step 1 validates only what debate-status.py lists); debate-status.py:160-161 (domain must be one of the six names, nothing else), :238-243 and :265-267 (hardened_default rules keyed on domain == 'security'), :427 ('security debate' gate tag), :467-470 (person gate on INCOMPLETE / disagreement, security only), :228-231 (verdict rubric must equal the request's domain, so an arbitrator cannot switch to the security rubric on its own; tests/lib/debate_cases.py DS-15 enforces that rejection); debate-protocol.md:98-100 ('set it honestly: auth, tokens, crypto, PII, CORS/CSRF, rate limits and tenant isolation are security'); debate_arbitrator.md:153-159. grep for any domain-fit or keyword check across .claude/hooks, .claude/commands, .claude/skills and tests: none; the only keyword list is autonomous.md:333, which governs the parent's auto-resolution defaults, not request labelling.
verdicts.note: Holds as stated. Every security control in the debate (security rubric with security_posture 35, hardened_default, the person gate, the 'security debate' gate tag that makes a forced gate need an acknowledgement) keys on a self-declared `domain`, and the only validation is the enum. Worse than the hat says: an arbitrator that notices the mislabel cannot correct it, because a verdict scored on the security rubric for an 'operations' request is rejected (debate-status.py:230-231), and nothing tells it to return BLOCKED instead. HIGH under the protocol scale: a check exists (the enum) but doesn't enforce the property the pipeline depends on, and under /autonomous a mislabelled rate-limit or session-TTL request is judged with no security criterion and never reaches a person. Not CRITICAL: it needs a requester mistake to trigger, and Wave 4's security_reviewer still sees the resulting code (a partial backstop for code-level consequences, not for the design choice itself). The moderator-side keyword check in the fix is the right place; mirroring it in debate-status.py request_problems as a warning would make it visible to the gate too.

verdicts.reproduction: Opened debate_arbitrator.md:222 (no check for an existing entry), remember.sh:71-100 (decide always allocates max+1 and appends; the only lookup is for --reverses), debate_moderator.md:129 (progress note -> re-spawn with 'Files already written: <paths>') and :155 ('Check its return as in step 4' applies it to the arbitrator), debate-status.py:306-311 (promoted() accepts any active block linking the verdict, or the decision_id's block). Scratch git repo with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set: ran the documented `remember.sh decide` command twice with `--link agent_state/debates/t5.verdict.json`: output 'D-001 recorded', 'D-002 recorded'; docs/DECISIONS.md then held two `status: active` blocks with the same link; promoted() returned True for decision_id D-001 and for D-002.
verdicts.note: Reproduced: remember.sh records a second active entry for the same verdict without complaint and the gate's promotion check passes on either. The trigger the hat describes (an arbitrator whose turn ends in a progress note after `remember.sh decide` but before `decision_id` is written, then re-spawned) is real but narrow; a moderator re-run (AI-10) that re-runs the arbitrator is a broader route to the same result. Contradiction needs the re-judgment to differ; agreement still leaves two active entries shown to every session. MEDIUM: a real gap in some situations, caught by nobody but with a reasonable workaround (the fix in the hat's own text). Same root problem as ARCH-07 (one active decision per topic depends on each writer remembering --reverses; nothing in remember.sh enforces it), so marked a duplicate of it; the arbitrator-side rule 'reuse the id of an active block that already links this verdict' should survive the fold as a second fix site.

verdicts.reproduction: Opened debate_moderator.md:195-205 (step 10 table keys on status + problems; rows for resolved/no problems, INCOMPLETE or no second opinion, invalid; none for stale or pending), :81 (already resolved -> return as is), :84-86 (stale -> run the debate), :282 and :285 (DoD); debate-status.py:383 (stale skips content checks), :444-473 (unpromoted, second-opinion problems, security INCOMPLETE/disagreement and default_taken mismatch go to `gate`, not `problems`); develop-orchestrator.md:1214-1232 (0c re-dispatches the moderator per pending/invalid topic). Scratch with tests/lib/make_debate.py: `--no-promote` -> {status: resolved, problems: [], gate: ['... has no D-NNN in docs/DECISIONS.md ...']}, `--check` exit 2; a close HIGH call (gap 0.3, MEDIUM) with a second opinion in the SAME order -> {status: resolved, problems: [], gate: ['second opinion didn't read the options in the reverse presentation order']}, exit 2; request_sha mis-copied -> {status: stale, problems: [], gate: [...]}, exit 2; request only -> {status: pending, problems: [], gate: [...]}.
verdicts.note: The core claim reproduces: in four states the gate blocks while `problems` is empty, and the step-10 table maps 'resolved, no problems' to COMPLETE, so the moderator's first line disagrees with the gate for an unpromoted verdict, a same-order second opinion and a default_taken mismatch. Narrowed on two points. (1) Stale is not a dead end: step 1 (:84-86) says a stale verdict re-runs the debate with PRIOR DECISION, so the 0c re-dispatch has a defined (if expensive) exit for that case; the 'already resolved, return as is' stall applies to the unpromoted and second-opinion-problem states, where the verdict is 'valid and current'. (2) The step-10 jq prints the whole topic object, `gate` included, so the information is in front of the moderator; the defect is that the rule ignores it, not that it can't see it. HIGH: the parent and the orchestrator act on this first line, it reports success for a topic the gate will block, and under /autonomous the result is a stall or (non-security, after three cycles) a force-gate that leaves the decision unpromoted, which is what promotion exists to prevent. Not CRITICAL because the gate itself still blocks and security states stop for a person. Same problem as ARCH-04 and TEST-14; marked a duplicate of ARCH-04.

verdicts.reproduction: Opened debate_moderator.md:88-99 (shuffle reorders ids; ids themselves are unchanged), debate-protocol.md:96 ('ids A-D. The order means nothing'), :59-60 (file names research-<id>.md / argument-<id>.md), debate_moderator.md:149 ('PRESENTATION ORDER: B A C'). WebSearch: Zheng et al., 'Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors' (ICLR 2024, arxiv 2309.03882) attributes selection bias primarily to token bias, 'where the model a priori assigns more probabilistic mass to specific option ID tokens (e.g., A/B/C/D)', separate from position. Opened T-007 task.md:20-29 and rubric.json:23: order_store and order_store_reversed swap the id labels along with position (A is the document store in request 1 and PostgreSQL in request 2, both presented A first).
verdicts.note: The premise is sourced (ID-token bias is documented as distinct from position bias) and the mechanism is as described: the shuffle hides reading order but the arbitrator still sees A-D labels that carry request order, and the reverse-order second opinion keeps the same labels, so a label preference would not surface as disagreement. Narrowed: the hat's 'test it in T-007' is already partly there, since the two data requests swap labels together with position (a judge favouring 'A' would pick the document store in request 1), though only on a MUST-decided case (AI-18 / TEST-28). The claim that requesters typically list their preferred option first is unverified; the repo's own fixtures put the winning option at A in one case (protocol :85) and at B in another (T-007 token_storage). The literature measures ID-token bias mostly on answer-by-letter MCQ, while the arbitrator scores criterion by criterion with anchors and cited reasons, which the rubric design already uses to damp halo and order effects. LOW: a hardening suggestion with no wrong instruction and no demonstrated failure; neutral aliases are cheap and would close it.

verdicts.reproduction: Opened debate_moderator.md:82-83 (already decided under another topic -> BLOCKED 'unless the request cites new evidence against it') and :84-86 (PRIOR DECISION passed only for a stale verdict on the same topic); debate_arbitrator.md:83-85 (--reverses is tied to 'PRIOR DECISION: D-NNN in your prompt', and applies 'whether you confirm the old choice or change it'), :35 (Required Reading: 'if new evidence contradicts one, append a reversing entry or escalate'), :216-219 (step 8 shows `[--reverses D-MMM] # when this overturns a prior decision`); remember.sh:83-92 (--reverses is the only mechanism that closes an active entry).
verdicts.note: The hand-off gap is real: the moderator identifies the prior D-NNN in step 1 and, when new evidence lets the debate run, hands the arbitrator nothing about it; the arbitrator's --reverses rule is written for the stale path. Narrowed because the contradictory case is partly covered elsewhere: the arbitrator is told to read the DECISIONS entries the request touches (:81) and step 8's generic '--reverses when this overturns a prior decision' plus Required Reading :35 would lead a careful arbitrator to reverse it, relying on it rediscovering an entry filed under a different topic by content. What nothing covers is the confirming case: a re-debate that upholds the old decision records a new active entry without reversing the old one (the stale path reverses 'whether you confirm or change'; the generic rule says 'overturns' only), leaving two active entries that agree. MEDIUM: a real gap with a workaround, two active entries shown to every session when it hits. The fix is one line in step 1. Overlaps ARCH-07's 'missed PRIOR DECISION' trigger; kept separate because the defect and the fix are in the moderator's hand-off, not in the ledger.
